# Commuter bicycle maintenance

Tyre pressure should be checked weekly. The sidewall of the tyre lists a
range, and a commuter riding on rough pavement works best near the lower end of
that range. Under-inflated tyres cause pinch punctures.

The chain is cleaned with a degreaser every month and lubricated with a wet
lubricant during the rainy season. A dry lubricant attracts less dirt in
summer. Wipe off the excess so that grit does not stick to the links.

Brake pads wear faster in winter. Replace them when the grooves in the rubber
are no longer visible. After fitting new pads, ride slowly and brake gently for
the first few kilometres to bed them in.

Every spring the wheels are checked for true by spinning them and watching the
gap at the brake blocks. A wobble of more than two millimetres means the
spokes need tension adjusted by a mechanic.
